newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends higher on month-end export deals.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends higher on month-end export deals.

text.p: The won finished firmer versus the dollar on Friday on the back of end-of-the-month export contracts and dollar inflow of funds from depository receipt issues, dealers said.
The won closed at 828.80 after opening at an intraday low of 829.50. It hit the high of 828.40.
Traders said sentiment was bullish toward the local unit as more month-end export deals were expected to be cashed in on Saturday.
However, speculation that the dollar would rebound early next month on import settlements prevented a sharp gain.
"The market has lost direction over uncertainty on how the dollar would move next month," said one trader. "The size of export deals on Saturday could determine the direction."
Dealers said some dollar selling by Cho Hung Bank after it issued $180 million global depository receipts (GDR) in London also helped to fuel good sentiment toward the won.
Traders expected the won to trade around the 828 level on Monday. The central bank set the base mid-rate at 828.70 for Monday against 828.80 for Friday.
